User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user in the Gamezone Pro application.

email.description: The email address of the user.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the user was created.

Admin.title: Admin
Admin.description: Represents an administrator of the Gamezone Pro application.

Tournament.title: Tournament
Tournament.description: Represents a BGMI tournament in the Gamezone Pro application.

gameName.description: The name of the game for the tournament.

entryFee.description: The entry fee for the tournament.

prizePool.description: The total prize pool for the tournament.

matchTime.description: The date and time of the tournament match.

roomId.description: The ID of the room for the tournament match.

roomPassword.description: The password for the tournament match room.

status.description: The current status of the tournament (e.g., Upcoming, Live, Completed).

commissionPercentage.description: The percentage of the prize pool taken as commission.

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the tournament was created.

Participant.title: Participant
Participant.description: Represents a user's participation in a tournament.

id.description: Unique identifier for the participant entry.

userId.description: Reference to the User entity. (Relationship: User 1:N Participant)

tournamentId.description: Reference to the Tournament entity. (Relationship: Tournament 1:N Participant)

result.description: The participant's result in the tournament (e.g., Winner, Participated).

joinedAt.description: Timestamp of when the user joined the tournament.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Represents a financial transaction in the user's wallet.

userId.description: Reference to the User entity. (Relationship: User 1:N Transaction)

type.description: The type of transaction (e.g., credit, debit).

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when the transaction occurred.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to address the 'auth/unauthorized-domain' Firebase error, enforce security, and ensure scalability. This error typically arises from domain misconfiguration in the Firebase Authentication settings. While this structure doesn't directly resolve the configuration issue, it facilitates simpler and more robust security rules once the domain is authorized.

**Authorization Independence:**  The design prioritizes authorization independence by denormalizing authorization data where needed. User roles are determined by the existence of documents in specific collections (e.g., `/roles_admin/{userId}`). This avoids the need for `get()` calls in security rules, which are known to break atomic operations.

**Structural Segregation:** The structure segregates data based on access requirements. User-specific data is stored under `/users/{userId}`, ensuring that only the user has access. Tournament data is stored in a top-level `/tournaments` collection. Membership in tournaments is tracked in `/users/{userId}/participants/{participantId}`, denormalizing data for authorization independence. This segregation simplifies the security rules for each collection.

**Access Modeling:** The structure uses path-based ownership for user data and the membership map pattern (denormalized) for collaborative data (tournaments). This approach provides a clear and consistent way to manage access control.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**  The structure supports secure `list` operations by avoiding reliance on server-side filtering in the rules. Tournament listing is secured using rules that ensure the data being listed is appropriate for the requesting user (e.g., a user can list tournaments they are participating in).

**Denormalization Strategy:** Crucially, the `participants` subcollection under each user document includes denormalized data relating to the user's participation in a given tournament. This approach is key for authorization independence and preventing rules from acting as filters. This addresses the core tenet of authorization independence by eliminating server `get()` calls.

In summary, this structure promotes clean security rules, ensures data integrity, facilitates scaling, and enhances debuggability.
